references.name: Friedrich von Hayek
references.connection:
Intellectual foundation; America's path mirrors Hayek's
  warning about government expansion destroying freedom

references.name: Ludwig von Mises
references.connection:
Austrian economics framework for malinvestment, business
  cycles, and sound money; core to Schiff's worldview

references.name: Murray Rothbard
references.desc: America's Great Depression; The Case Against the Fed
references.connection: Revisionist account of 1930s and critique of Fed central banking

references.name: Henry Hazlitt
references.connection: Foundational layperson economics from Austrian school perspective

references.name: Irwin Schiff
references.desc: How an Economy Grows and Why It Doesn't

references.name: Alan Greenspan
references.desc: Fed Chairman 1987-2006; essay "Gold and Economic Freedom" (1966)
references.connection:
Primary antagonist — a man who understood sound money perfectly
  and then spent 20 years destroying it

references.name: James Turk
references.desc: GoldMoney.com; The Coming Collapse of the Dollar
references.connection:
Co-aligns on gold thesis; Schiff recommends GoldMoney as
  trusted online gold storage platform

references.name: Jim Rogers
references.connection:
Shares commodity and Asian investment thesis; one of the
  "legendary investors" advocating exit from USD

references.name: Milton Friedman
references.connection:
Referenced in recommended reading; shared belief in free
  markets though Schiff is Austrian, not Chicago School

references.name: James Madison
references.connection:
Quoted on dangers of democracy vs. republic; supports
  Schiff's argument that the founders intended limited government

references.name: Benjamin Franklin
references.connection:
"A republic if you can keep it" — invoked as critique
  of democratic drift and erosion of constitutional limits

references.name: Charles Kindleberger
references.connection:
Historical record of financial bubbles; background for
  Schiff's framework on credit cycles
